name: Hereditary Breast and Ovarian Cancer Syndrome (BRCA1/BRCA2)

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: National Comprehensive Cancer Network (NCCN) BRCA Testing Criteria

criteria.description: Multiple family members with breast cancer diagnosed before age 50
Personal history of ovarian, fallopian tube, or primary peritoneal cancer
Male breast cancer in the individual or family
Identification of pathogenic BRCA1 or BRCA2 variant by genetic testing

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Identification of a pathogenic BRCA1 or BRCA2 variant by genetic testing, or meeting multiple major clinical criteria such as early-onset breast cancer and family history of ovarian cancer
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing is the definitive diagnostic method; clinical criteria guide testing eligibility.

rare.symptomName: Male prostate cancer with BRCA2 mutation
Neurological symptoms secondary to paraneoplastic syndromes

laboratory: Abnormal tumor markers depending on cancer type
imaging: Pelvic ultrasound or MRI detecting ovarian masses
CT scan for staging pancreatic or other cancers
other: Family history of breast, ovarian, pancreatic, or prostate cancer
Histopathology showing high-grade serous carcinoma in ovaries

distinguishingFeatures: TP53 mutation instead of BRCA mutations
Broader spectrum of cancers including sarcomas and brain tumors
Presence of multiple hamartomas and mucocutaneous lesions
Increased risk of breast cancer but also thyroid and endometrial cancers

redFlags: Multiple family members with breast or ovarian cancer
Male breast cancer in the family
references: NCCN Clinical Practice Guidelines in Oncology: Genetic/Familial High-Risk Assessment: Breast, Ovarian, and Pancreatic, Version 3.2024
Miki Y, Swensen J, Shattuck-Eidens D, et al. A strong candidate for the breast and ovarian cancer susceptibility gene BRCA1. Science. 1994.
King MC, Marks JH, Mandell JB. Breast and ovarian cancer risks due to inherited mutations in BRCA1 and BRCA2. Science. 2003.
